new_integration_decision: The proposed lock-compatible spawn test can pass vacuously if the second process starts late and reads only after the first append. Treat a PASS without observed competing admission or independently demonstrated serialization as INCONCLUSIVE, not proof of cross-process safety. Existing runner publishes latest/audit/anata as three independent atomic replaces, so final timestamp equality alone cannot close reader-coherence gate.

no_network_test_contract.scope: A lane only; use temporary archive and spawn processes, no live collectors
steps: Use multiprocessing.get_context('spawn') and module-level child target; install instrumentation inside each child (parent monkeypatches do not propagate under spawn). Start both workers from a shared parent gate and record each child's reached-admission event, read checkpoint, completion and exception/exit code.

With identical valid observation IDs, delay A after its archive read. Wait for B to reach a pre-read or post-read checkpoint when unlocked; if B cannot reach the read because a lock serializes it, release A after a bounded wait and require B to finish. Do not require both to cross a barrier inside a possible critical section.

Classify run as demonstrated overlap only if B actually reached the competing read before A appended; otherwise require independent serialization evidence. If neither is observed, label INCONCLUSIVE and never treat the archive row count alone as a concurrency PASS.

On a demonstrated overlap or proven serialization, assert exactly one valid JSONL record and total append count 1; test distinct IDs (both survive, valid JSONL), and sequential replay (0 new rows). Propagate child errors and fail on timeout.

Keep generation-identity B-wins, same-clock distinct-evidence and supported-reader snapshot coherence as separate targeted tests. Require actual targeted and full Capital Flow pytest exit codes and logs on the exact SHA.
